name: Pflach
kurzbeschreibung: Cozy residential community near Reutte with direct access to the Naturbad and the surrounding hiking trails.
text:
Overview

Pflach is situated in the expansive valley basin of Reutte in the Außerfern region at an altitude of 840 metres, located along the eastern banks of the wild Lech River immediately north of the district capital Reutte. This active nature park municipality is home to approximately 1,550 residents and spans 13.8 square kilometres within the Tyrolean Lech Nature Park, right at the foot of the massive limestone peak of Mount Säuling (2,047 m) in the Ammergau Alps. Only a few kilometres separate Pflach from the Bavarian border and the world-renowned royal castles of Neuschwanstein and Hohenschwangau near Füssen. Geographically, Pflach captivates visitors through the dramatic contrast between its ecologically precious riverside gravel beds – along the last wild river in the Northern Alps – and sheer alpine precipices. The village harmoniously blends international bird conservation with outdoor recreation, cultural history, and superb connectivity.

History

The name Pflach originates from the Middle High German vlach, signifying a flat riverside meadow; its earliest written record dates to 1275 under the name Plech. In antiquity, the historic Roman trading and military road Via Claudia Augusta crossed the municipal area. Pflach experienced an era of widespread industrial prominence in the 16th century: following medieval iron mining on Mount Säuling, the Augsburg merchant family Höchstätter founded West Tyrol's sole brass foundry here in 1515. The foundry processed calamine from Nassereith and copper from Schwaz and Kitzbühel into fine brass; in 1606, the complex was converted into a large grain mill (Hüttenmühle). The Gothic St. Ulrich's Chapel at the Hüttenmühle, built in 1515, still preserves its precious carved winged altarpiece. In the village centre, the Baroque Church of the Epiphany (Heilige Drei Könige), erected around 1720, forms an attractive cultural centerpiece.

Getting There

Pflach boasts an extraordinarily convenient geographic position straddling the Austrian-Bavarian border. Motorists arrive toll-free from Germany via motorway A7 and Füssen across the border in just ten minutes; from the south, federal highway B179 (Fernpass route) leads straight to the dedicated Reutte-Nord/Pflach exit. Rail travellers enjoy their own station, Pflach railway station, on the historic Außerfern Railway (Außerfernbahn), served hourly by regional trains running between Kempten in the Allgäu, Pfronten, Reutte, and Garmisch-Partenkirchen, offering seamless connections to Munich and Innsbruck. In addition, VVT regional bus route 150 links Pflach frequently with Reutte, Füssen, and Vils. Cyclists access the village directly along the Lech River Cycle Path and the Roman Via Claudia Augusta route.

Tips

An internationally acclaimed nature highlight is the Pflacher Auen wetland reserve with its 20-metre-high wooden birdwatching tower at Kohlplatz: designated as a Natura 2000 protected sanctuary, these alluvial riparian forests provide breeding and resting grounds for over two-thirds of all bird species recorded in Tyrol; an interactive bird educational trail details the habitat of kingfishers and sandpipers. Adjacent lies peaceful Lake Hüttenmühlsee with the historic 1515 Hüttenmühl Chapel. Long-distance hikers can join the Lechweg trail on its final stage leading through Pflach towards the Lechfall waterfall in Füssen. Seasoned mountaineers can summit Mount Säuling (2,047 m) via the alpine Säulinghaus hut (1,720 m), rewarding climbers with breathtaking aerial views of Neuschwanstein Castle and Bavarian lakes. Just five kilometres south lies the Ehrenberg Castle ensemble with the highline179 suspension bridge.
